column1: # Game profile of Sky Force Reloaded (Switch, base game v0 + update 1.1.1 = v1). Plays on Android (android.tsv)
# Infinite Dreams' Unity game (player 2017.4.4f1, IL2CPP) on NintendoWare NVN, FMOD for sound, SDK 4.5.0; subsdk0 is the SDK's movie library (the opening movie).
# Checked on the device: the build IDs of the three modules, the NPDM's system resource (none) and the RomFS (111 files, 0.73 GB: the UnityFS bundles and
# data.unity3d under Data/, plus Data/Managed and Data/Resources)
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk0 (the movie library, which main imports from), sdk
# The NPDM declares no system resource, so the game has no virtual address memory: Unity sets a heap of the pool less 64 MB of used memory, 3.3 GB, in the 3.25 GB
# heap region of a 4 GB block. The application pool is the Switch's 3285 MB
# 3,050 shaders, Shader objects in the UnityFS bundles and data.unity3d under Data/. Unity 2017 writes no type trees, so the split needs unityfs.py's tree for the
# type hash these objects carry (266d5311...): without it the split stops at "without type trees" and none of them is translated. The ComputeShader objects in
# 'unity default resources' carry a 2017 hash unityfs.py has no layout for yet: the split says so in red and leaves their kernels out (the game plays without them)
# the rewritten modules need more than the default 64 MB of used memory (74 MB)
